# putty

**The GUI serial terminal hams reach for, with saved sessions**

- **Version recorded:** 0.83
- **Categories:** `serial-terminals`, `workstation`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.chiark.greenend.org.uk/~sgtatham/putty/>

## What it does

PuTTY: a graphical terminal for serial lines (and SSH/telnet). On Linux its serial mode is the draw -- pick a device and speed, save the session, reconnect in a click.

## Why you would want it

The de facto GUI serial console for radio work: rig debug ports, TNC configuration, GPS at a raw baud rate. Saved sessions per device beat retyping stty incantations.

## Before it will work

Access to the serial device -- membership of the `dialout` group, which the workstation profile arranges. A programming cable or rig data port.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install putty --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `putty`

## Known problems

`ssh` makes PuTTY's network side redundant on Linux; it is carried for the serial side. Needs `dialout` for the serial device -- the workstation profile adds you.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
